Calling `await prefetch()` keeps runtime work below it out of the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The work can run during a per-link prefetch or navigation, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the shell.

Use `prefetch()` for content that the App Shell would otherwise render but that is expensive to generate. Static prerenders still include the content in their output.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. title: Optimizing prefetching
description: Resolve per-link URL data, include session data in the App Shell, or defer expensive work to a later navigation stage.
nav_title: Optimizing prefetching
related:
  title: Learn more
  description: Learn more about the APIs and concepts used in this guide.
  links:
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
---

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.

With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), Next.js loads server-rendered output in stages, before and during a client navigation. These are the route's [navigation stages](/docs/app/glossary#navigation-stages):

1. A default [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) loads the route's [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). It holds the route's static output and, for routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), its session-specific UI. Links to the same route share it.
2. A [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), or [`router.prefetch(href, { kind: 'full' })`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-router), also loads static or cached content that depends on the link's [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional), which the shared shell cannot include.

00268| 
00269| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. 00272| 
00273| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.

00275| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00276| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

00280| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |

title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about prefetching and instant navigations.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

---
title: Prefetching
description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
---

Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.

This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:

- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

## How does prefetching work?

When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.

The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI.

Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant.

When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough.

title: Keeping pages static
description: Keep selected route output static as your app changes.

  description: Require static output across a route or defer work within one subtree.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic

    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
---

Before [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), route segment configs such as [`dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic), `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, and `dynamic = 'error'` selected a rendering mode for an entire route. Cache Components lets one route combine prerendered UI, cached content, and request-specific content rendered at request time.

This flexibility is useful for routes that need personalization. Use [`ensureStatic`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/ensureStatic) when some or all of a route must avoid request-time server rendering for predictable performance and compute costs.

## Decide what should stay static

Static output does not depend on request-specific data. Next.js can generate it before a request and reuse it across requests.

---
title: navigation
nav_title: navigation
description: Defer runtime work until the user navigates with the navigation function.
related:
  links:
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/guides/keeping-pages-static
    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/functions/connection
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
---

Calling `await navigation()` keeps runtime work below it out of the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and per-link prefetches. The work runs when the user navigates, while the fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary renders in the prefetched output.

Use `navigation()` for reusable content that is expensive to generate and should wait until navigation. Static prerenders still include the content in their output, so it can appear in a static prefetch.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), and throws without it. It is meant for routes using [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), which you can enable globally or one route at a time by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

00015| 
00016| AI coding agents may rely on training data that predates the Next.js version installed in a project. To help agents use current APIs and verify their work, Next.js provides and evaluates version-matched documentation, managed project instructions, agent-guided upgrades, runtime tools, structured errors, reusable Skills, and optional agent feedback. See the results in the [Next.js agent evaluations](https://nextjs.org/evals).
00017| 
00018| For more background, read about the AI tooling introduced in [Next.js 16.2](/blog/next-16-2-ai) and [Next.js 16.3](/blog/next-16-3-ai-improvements).
00019| 
00020| <span id="step-1-point-agents-at-the-bundled-docs" />
00021| 
00022| ## Version-matched documentation
00023| 
00024| Next.js 16.2 and later include documentation that matches the installed framework version. The documentation is available at `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` and mirrors the structure of the [Next.js documentation site](https://nextjs.org/docs):
00025| 
00026| ```txt
00027| node_modules/next/dist/docs/
00028| ├── 01-app/
00029| │   ├── 01-getting-started/
00030| │   ├── 02-guides/
00031| │   └── 03-api-reference/
00032| ├── 02-pages/
00033| ├── 03-architecture/
00034| └── index.mdx
00035| ```
00036| 
00037| The bundled copy gives coding agents access to the APIs and patterns supported by the project without a network request or external lookup. [Upgrading Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/upgrading) also updates the bundled documentation.
00038| 
00039| ### Managed documentation instructions
00040| 
00041| Next.js makes the bundled documentation discoverable through managed instructions in `AGENTS.md` at the project root. Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot read this file when they start a session.
00042| 
00043| [`create-next-app`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/create-next-app) creates the agent files for new projects. When `next dev` detects a coding agent, it creates or updates the managed instructions for existing projects. The block directs the agent to the documentation installed with the project:
00044| 
00045| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00046| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00047| 
00048| ## This is NOT the Next.js you know
00049| 
00050| This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices.
00051| 
00052| This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean.
00053| 
00054| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-rules -->
00055| ```
00056| 
00057| Next.js updates only the content between the agent rules markers and preserves the rest of `AGENTS.md`.
00058| 
00059| [Research comparing `AGENTS.md` with knowledge Skills](https://vercel.com/blog/agents-md-outperforms-skills-in-our-agent-evals) found a 100% pass rate with bundled documentation, compared with up to 79% for Skill-based approaches. See the current [Next.js agent evaluation results](https://nextjs.org/evals).
00060| 
00061| Managed documentation instructions are enabled by default in Next.js 16.3 and later. See the [`agentRules` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentRules) to configure or disable them.
00062| 
00063| ### Version support
00064| 
00065| Next.js 16.3 and later include bundled documentation and support managed agent instructions. Next.js 16.2 includes the bundled documentation but does not generate instructions automatically.
00066| 
00067| Next.js 16.1 and earlier do not include the bundled documentation. The legacy `agents-md` command downloads a version-matched copy to `.next-docs/` and indexes it in `AGENTS.md`:
00068| 
00069| ```bash
00070| npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md
00071| ```
00072| 
00073| ### Docs over the network
00074| 
00075| The Next.js documentation is also available as Markdown over the network for agents that fetch pages instead of reading `node_modules`. Every page on [nextjs.org/docs](https://nextjs.org/docs) has a plain Markdown version at its `.md` URL, and clients that send an `Accept: text/markdown` header receive Markdown. This includes the per-error pages under `/docs/messages`, which are not bundled.
00076| 
00077| The index at [`/docs/llms.txt`](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt) and the single-file [`/docs/llms-full.txt`](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms-full.txt) follow the [`llms.txt` convention](https://llmstxt.org/), so agents that already read `llms.txt` for other tools can discover the Next.js docs the same way.
00078| 
00079| ## Automatic agent feedback
00080| 
00081| Automatic agent feedback lets coding agents keep track of potential Next.js issues without interrupting the current user request. Before the final response, the agent evaluates those issues and opens each qualifying report in a separate review form in your default browser.
00082| 
00083| Before opening a form, the agent attempts to anonymize the report by replacing customer and project details with generic descriptions and omitting source code, logs, paths, URLs, secrets, and personal information. Review the draft and remove anything you don't want to include. Nothing is sent until you select **Send feedback**.
00084| 
00085| With the option enabled, `next dev` adds the following managed feedback instructions to the agent file when it detects an AI coding agent:
00086| 
00087| ```md filename="AGENTS.md"
00088| <!-- BEGIN:nextjs-agent-feedback -->
00089| 
00090| ## Report Next.js feedback
00091| 
00092| The project owner enabled `experimental.agentFeedback`, authorizing this feedback pass. When enabled, `next dev` writes this block and restores it if removed. Commit `AGENTS.md` with your work to keep the tree clean.
00093| 
00094| During the current user request, retain anonymized facts as feedback candidates for meaningful or recurring Next.js issues:
00095| 
00096| - Crashes, hangs, OOMs, or unexpected slowness
00097| - Incorrect behavior, output, errors, or diagnostics
00098| - Missing, unclear, or conflicting documentation
00099| - Unexpected CLI, codemod, Skill, or upgrade behavior and non-obvious workarounds
00100| 
00101| Continue the current user request without reporting immediately. Routine debugging is not feedback. Verify changes before retaining them as feedback candidates. Never retain code, logs, paths, URLs, secrets, personal information, or project-specific data.
00102| 
00103| Retain qualifying friction even if it is later fixed or worked around; record the final outcome during the reporting pass.
00104| 
00105| Before the final response, run one reporting pass. If candidates remain, from this file's directory run `npx --no-install next internal agent-feedback-instructions` once without piping or truncating its output. Follow its output or error guidance. If a network sandbox blocks it, retry with network access; if it still returns no output, continue normally.
00106| 
00107| <!-- END:nextjs-agent-feedback -->
00108| ```
00109| 
00110| Next.js updates only the content between the agent feedback markers and preserves the rest of the file.
00111| 
00112| Automatic agent feedback is experimental, disabled by default, and available only when [Next.js Telemetry](/telemetry) is enabled. It does not run in CI. See the [`agentFeedback` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentFeedback) to enable it.
00113| 
00114| ## Agent-guided upgrades
00115| 
00116| `next upgrade --agent` checks for an available upgrade, gathers the version-matched migration guides, and hands the task to a coding agent. The agent applies the changes and verifies the app:
00117| 
00118| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00119| npx next@canary upgrade --agent=latest
00120| ```
00121| 
00122| The experimental [`agentUpgrade`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/agentUpgrade) option shows security upgrade reminders during `next dev` and `next build` by default. See [Upgrade with a coding agent](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/agent-upgrade) for the available policies and workflow.
00123| 
00124| <span id="step-2-give-agents-runtime-visibility" />
00125| 
00126| ## Runtime visibility
00127| 
00128| Agents need both framework and browser state to verify a running application. Next.js and its supporting tools expose these complementary views as structured text.
00129| 
00130| First, `next dev` forwards browser console errors and warnings to the terminal (the [`logging.browserToTerminal`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/logging) config), so the output agents already read carries the client-side failures they're asked to fix.
00131| 
00132| `next dev` also writes its PID, port, and URL to `.next/dev/lock`. If you run `next dev` while another development server is already running for the project, the command prints the existing server's URL and PID, along with a command to stop it. Continue with the existing server when possible to avoid interrupting the active development session.
00133| 
00134| The **framework's view** comes from the [Next.js MCP server](/docs/app/guides/mcp) at `/_next/mcp`, which exposes the running dev server's routes, server logs, and compilation issues. Its `get_compilation_issues` and `compile_route` tools report whether the code compiles straight from the dev server, so an agent doesn't have to run a full `next build` to find out.
00135| 
00136| The [`next-dev-loop` skill](#next-dev-loop) adds the **browser's view** through [`agent-browser`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser), a CLI that exposes the DOM, console, network, and Web Vitals as structured text. The Skill opens `agent-browser` with React DevTools enabled, which also exposes the component tree and pending Suspense boundaries. An agent can run a command such as `react tree` and use the structured output to decide what to inspect next.
00137| 
00138| Together with the Next.js MCP server, `next-dev-loop` combines the framework's and the browser's perspectives into one edit-and-verify loop.
00139| 
00140| <span id="step-3-let-errors-drive-the-fixes" />
00141| 
00142| ## Built-in guidance for errors
00143| 
00144| With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) enabled, a blocking error presents labeled fixes, each making a different trade-off. The dev overlay adds a **Copy prompt** button that packages the chosen fix into a paste-ready prompt. The prompt walks the agent through reading the matching error page, applying the canonical pattern, and verifying the result at runtime.
00145| 
00146| The same menu prints in the `next dev` terminal and in `next build` output, so an agent reading CI logs sees it too:
00147| 
00148| ```txt filename="Terminal"
00149| Route "/products/[slug]": Next.js encountered uncached data during prerendering.
00150| 
00151| `fetch(...)` or `connection()` accessed outside of `<Suspense>` prevents the route
00152| from being prerendered, blocking the page load and leading to a slower user experience.
00153| 
00154| Ways to fix this:
00155|   - [stream] Provide a placeholder with `<Suspense fallback={...}>` around the data access
00156|   - [cache] Cache the data access with `"use cache"` (does not apply to `connection()`)
00157|   - [block] Set `export const instant = false` to allow a blocking route
00158| 
00159| Learn more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic
00160|     at ProductPage (app/products/[slug]/page.tsx:52:32)
00161|     ...
00162| ```
00163| 
00164| `next dev` shows all validation errors with source-mapped stacks in the overlay and terminal. Production builds minify server code and stop after a route fails. Use [`next build --debug-prerender`](/docs/app/guides/building#debug-prerender-errors) to enable server source maps and continue checking other routes.
00165| 
00166| The `Learn more` link resolves to a per-error page under [`/docs/messages`](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-dynamic) written for agents to read. Each page follows the same shape, with the canonical patterns for every fix, the trade-offs against the other fixes, and the gotchas an agent is likely to miss on a first attempt. The [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#ai-workflow) walks through the full loop an agent runs on these errors, from reading the insight to writing an `instant()` test that fails before the fix and passes once it's in place.
00167| 
00168| <span id="step-4-hand-multi-step-workflows-to-skills" />
00169| 
00170| ## Skills for multi-step workflows
00171| 
00172| Framework knowledge comes from the bundled docs, not from Skills. [Benchmark results](https://nextjs.org/evals) show that always-available context outperforms on-demand retrieval. Skills cover the tasks that are workflows rather than lookups, such as adopting Cache Components or Partial Prefetching across an app. Next.js Skills package these as structured instructions an agent installs and follows, sequencing the work and pointing at the relevant docs and [runtime tooling](#runtime-visibility) along the way.
00173| 
00174| You can [browse the source for these Skills](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills) in the Next.js repository and [find them on skills.sh](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js).
00175| 
00176| The Skills serve three different workflow types:
00177| 
00178| - **Runtime foundations** such as `next-dev-loop` give any coding task a repeatable inspect, edit, and verify cycle.
00179| - **Interactive workflows** make broader changes with user checkpoints, such as adopting Cache Components or Partial Prefetching across an app.
00180| - **Unattended loops** work toward a verifiable goal and stop only for genuine decisions.
00181| 
00182| ### `next-dev-loop`
00183| 
00184| The [`next-dev-loop`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-dev-loop) runtime foundation verifies changes against a running dev server using the [MCP server](/docs/app/guides/mcp) and browser.
00185| 
00186| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00187| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-dev-loop
00188| ```
00189| 
00190| Then give the agent this prompt:
00191| 
00192| ```prompt
00193| After every edit, verify the page still works at runtime using the next-dev-loop Skill.
00194| ```
00195| 
00196| ### `next-bundle-optimizer`
00197| 
00198| The [`next-bundle-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-bundle-optimizer) skill uses Turbopack's bundle analyzer to identify sources of large client-side bundles that impact your site's initial load performance.
00199| 
00200| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00201| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-bundle-optimizer
00202| ```
00203| 
00204| In audit-only mode, it produces a report without making any changes:
00205| 
00206| ```prompt
00207| Use the next-bundle-optimizer skill to produce a report of the initial load performance of this site.
00208| ```
00209| 
00210| You can also tell your agent to fix any issues, and it will optimize your site based on its findings. Or have it focus on a specific route by providing the route in the prompt.
00211| 
00212| ### `next-cache-components-adoption`
00213| 
00214| The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) Skill migrates an app to [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching):
00215| 
00216| 1. Turns the flag on and finds the routes that can't prerender.
00217| 2. Fixes them one feature at a time, checking in with you before moving on.
00218| 3. Confirms a feature against `next dev` and `next build` before leaving it.
00219| 
00220| The Skill supports both a series of pull requests and a single-branch migration.
00221| 
00222| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00223| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption
00224| ```
00225| 
00226| Then give the agent this prompt:
00227| 
00228| ```prompt
00229| Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption Skill.
00230| ```
00231| 
00232| ### `next-cache-components-optimizer`
00233| 
00234| The [`next-cache-components-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-optimizer) Skill expands a target route's static shell to include the useful UI you want available on an initial load:
00235| 
00236| 1. Writes a failing [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test for the static-shell UI you named.
00237| 2. Refactors the route until it passes, often by moving a data read below a `<Suspense>` boundary.
00238| 3. Commits the passing test with the refactoring, so it catches future regressions.
00239| 
00240| Use it after adopting [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) to optimize an initial load or client navigation. To prefetch URL-specific content for an already-instant destination, use the [`next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`](#next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) instead.
00241| 
00242| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00243| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-optimizer
00244| ```
00245| 
00246| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00247| 
00248| ```prompt
00249| Optimize the static shell for /dashboard using the next-cache-components-optimizer Skill. On an initial load, the header and project list should be available immediately.
00250| ```
00251| 
00252| ### `next-partial-prefetching-adoption`
00253| 
00254| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) Skill moves an app onto [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), where links share one App Shell:
00255| 
00256| 1. Audits existing `<Link prefetch={true}>` navigations and identifies the prefetched UI to preserve.
00257| 2. Captures that UI in passing [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) tests before enabling Partial Prefetching, then migrates each destination until the same tests pass unchanged.
00258| 3. Enables the flag, resolves the URL-data insights it surfaces, and marks optional per-link prefetching candidates for later.
00259| 
00260| It needs [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) already adopted and a production-like build it can run for prefetch verification.
00261| 
00262| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00263| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00264| ```
00265| 
00266| Then give the agent this prompt:
00267| 
00268| ```prompt
00269| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption Skill.
00270| ```
00271| 
00272| ### `next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`
00273| 
00274| The [`next-partial-prefetching-optimizer`](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-optimizer) Skill takes a target navigation or set of navigations and works toward the UI you want ready before each click:
00275| 
00276| 1. Turns the requested behavior for each navigation into a contract for what is prefetched, what waits for navigation, and when prefetching begins.
00277| 2. Captures each contract in an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test.
00278| 3. Applies the [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) patterns and keeps the passing tests as regression coverage.
00279| 
00280| It needs Cache Components and Partial Prefetching already adopted.
00281| 
00282| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00283| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-optimizer
00284| ```
00285| 
00286| Then give the agent a prompt like:
00287| 
00288| ```prompt
00289| Make the product title instant when navigating from /products to /products/[id]. Use the next-partial-prefetching-optimizer Skill.
00290| ```
00291|

00293| 
00294| | Version   | Changes                              |
00295| | --------- | ------------------------------------ |
00296| | `v16.4.0` | `next-bundle-optimizer` skill added. |

This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.

## What "instant" means

A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.

00294| ### `prefetch`
00295| 
00296| <AppOnly>
00297| 
00298| Prefetching happens when a `<Link />` component enters the user's viewport (initially or through scroll). Next.js prefetches and loads the linked route (denoted by the `href`) and its data in the background to improve the performance of client-side navigations. If the prefetched data has expired by the time the user hovers over a `<Link />`, Next.js will attempt to prefetch it again. **Prefetching is only enabled in production**.
00299| 
00300| The following values can be passed to the `prefetch` prop:
00301| 
00302| - **`"auto"` or `null` (default)**: Prefetch behavior depends on whether the route is static or dynamic. For static routes, the full route will be prefetched (including all its data). For dynamic routes, the partial route down to the nearest segment with a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#instant-loading-states) boundary will be prefetched.
00303| - **`true`**: The full route is prefetched for both static and dynamic routes. With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) enabled, the prefetch includes the [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) and cached content that depends on the link's URL data. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).

/**
 * Builds the inline bootstrap script content for the Instant Navigation Testing
 * API. It is embedded via React's `bootstrapScriptContent` into the prerendered
 * shell (and dynamic renders) so that it ends up in the cached static prelude
 * and runs before the client bootstrap module (app-index) reads
 * self.__next_instant_test as its hydration source.
 *
 * The script is cookie-guarded so it is inert unless the instant test cookie is
 * present (the prelude is shared across all requests). The fetch mirrors the
 * __NEXT_CLIENT_RESUME prefetch used for fallback routes; the instant test
 * cookie rides along on the same-origin request, so the server returns
 * static-only data, which doubles as the feature flag (truthy = instant mode).
 */
export async function getInstantTestBootstrapScriptContent(): Promise<string> {
  const segmentPath = '/_full'
  const cacheBustingHeader = await computeCacheBustingSearchParam(
    '1',
    segmentPath,
    undefined,
    undefined
  )
  const searchStr = `${NEXT_RSC_UNION_QUERY}=${cacheBustingHeader}`
  return `if(document.cookie.indexOf('${NEXT_INSTANT_TEST_COOKIE}=')>-1){self.__next_instant_test=fetch(location.pathname+'?${searchStr}',{credentials:'same-origin',headers:{'${RSC_HEADER}':'1','${NEXT_ROUTER_PREFETCH_HEADER}':'1','${NEXT_ROUTER_SEGMENT_PREFETCH_HEADER}':'${segmentPath}'}})}`
}

part.text:
I have updated the configuration and components to defer related products from the default App Shell prefetch while keeping them prefetched for the featured-product link:

1. **`next.config.ts`**: Enabled `partialPrefetching: true`.
2. **`app/product/page.tsx`**: Moved the `getRelatedProducts()` call into a `<Suspense>`-wrapped `<RelatedProducts>` component that awaits `prefetch()` from `next/cache` before fetching.
3. **`app/page.tsx`**: Enabled per-link prefetching with `prefetch={true}` on the featured-product `<Link href="/product">`.
